findings.title: Timeout can still become a false safe terminal result
findings.trigger: The Host timeout fires, its adapter or root process closes, but a detached nested writer remains alive or its stop identity cannot be proved.
findings.impact: The implementation can satisfy the listed task checks while still publishing `failure_type: timeout`, releasing the fence, and permitting a second writer against roots that may still be changing.
findings.evidence: D1R-02 enumerates outer-worker loss, live/stopped inner writers, cancellation acknowledgement, and stale identity, while D1R-04 requires only proven-stopped cancellation compatibility. Neither criterion or its evidence requires the timeout branch promised by D1-AC02 to prove the same writer boundary before returning a terminal timeout.
findings.suggestion: Add one explicit nested-writer timeout RED/GREEN case to D1R-02 and the narrow verification: a proven-stopped boundary may return `timeout`; an alive or unprovable boundary must return `outcome_unknown`, retain the fence, and remain non-retryable.

findings.title: Missing Host receipt is not proof that the one-call budget is unconsumed
findings.trigger: The coordinator or transport is interrupted after the selected-Host request is dispatched but before the planned raw or redacted receipt is durably published.
findings.impact: A fresh session can interpret the absent receipt as an unconsumed allowance and issue a second provider call, exceeding the exact one-call grant and obscuring whether the first attempt produced effects.
findings.evidence: Fresh-session recovery says to inspect the planned raw receipt path before deciding whether the live-call budget remains, but the plan has no pre-dispatch reservation or rule that an indeterminate dispatched attempt consumes the budget. Receipt absence therefore cannot distinguish never-launched from launched-with-unknown-outcome.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the existing delegation attempt identity and atomically record `dispatched` plus budget consumption before the provider request. If no bound terminal receipt arrives, retain `outcome_unknown`, treat the call as consumed, and prohibit retry until an explicit new grant or authoritative proof of non-dispatch exists.

positive_observations: The plan correctly routes unproved writer termination to launcher-side `failure_type: outcome_unknown` without adding a model-facing status.
The plan preserves the writer fence on uncertainty, forbids TTL deletion, and explicitly prohibits automatic retry or fallback.
limitations: This is a plan-mode review; no runtime implementation diff or live selected-Host qualification result exists yet.
